disasterDrill.title: Disaster Drill
disasterDrill.body: Run a no-signing rehearsal for common recovery failures using your descriptor and checklist answers.

ds1.title: I lost my hardware wallet
ds1.body: Check whether the backup materials and written notes would let you replace the device.

ds2.title: My laptop died
ds2.body: Check whether the wallet can be rebuilt without the old computer.

ds3.title: My wallet app disappeared
ds3.body: Check whether a neutral watch-only wallet can be restored from the descriptor.

ds4.title: I have my seed but not my wallet file
ds4.body: Check whether the derivation details and software notes are documented.

ds5.title: I have my descriptor but not all signers
ds5.body: Check whether the remaining signers still meet the multisig threshold.

ds6.title: One multisig signer is unavailable
ds6.body: Check the M-of-N survivability model without creating or signing a PSBT.

ms2of3.title: 2-of-3 multisig survivability
ms2of3.body: Simulate losing one signer, two signers, and the descriptor backup.

ms3of5.title: 3-of-5 multisig survivability
ms3of5.body: Simulate losing one signer, two signers, and the descriptor backup.

missingSigner.title: Missing signer drill
missingSigner.body: Pick one signer to lose and check whether the remaining signers still meet quorum on regtest or Signet.

ds7.title: My spouse needs to recover
ds7.body: Run a fake-funds PSBT signing drill that another person could follow.

ds8.title: I need to verify my hardware wallet can still sign
ds8.body: Move a test PSBT to a signer by file or QR and confirm the destination on the device.

ds9.title: I want to test a PSBT signing workflow
ds9.body: Create, sign, import, and finalize a test PSBT without touching real funds.

ds10.title: I want to simulate restoring on a clean machine
ds10.body: Use the same file or QR signing path you would need on a replacement computer.

readinessCheck.title: Run a Readiness Check
readinessCheck.body: Walk through a guided audit of your wallet's output descriptor.

wizard.saveAndQuitNote: Nothing you enter is saved between sessions.
wizard.sampleNote: This is a documented test-network descriptor, loaded so you can walk through the flow without your own data.

walletType.title: What kind of wallet are you checking?
walletType.help: Pick the closest match. If you are not sure, choose “I'm not sure” and we will work it out from your descriptor.

inputMethod.title: How would you like to provide your descriptor?
inputMethod.help: Your output descriptor is public wallet metadata — not a seed phrase and not a private key.

descriptor.title: Paste or load your descriptor
descriptor.help: Paste your output descriptor below. Never paste seed words, private keys, or passphrases.
descriptor.label: Output descriptor
descriptor.fileNote: You can paste your descriptor, choose a file, or drag a file onto the box below.
descriptor.dropHere: Drag a descriptor file here, or use the buttons above.
descriptor.warnNote: This looks like it could contain secret-like text, but we could not confirm it. If you are sure this is only a public descriptor, confirm below to continue.
descriptor.warnConfirm: I confirm this is not a real secret

knownAddress.title: Add a known receive address
knownAddress.help: Optional. If you provide an address you know belongs to this wallet, the check can compare it against the addresses derived from your descriptor.
knownAddress.label: Known receive address

passphrase.title: Does this wallet use a BIP39 passphrase?
passphrase.help: We never ask for the passphrase itself — only whether one exists. A forgotten passphrase is one of the most common reasons a recovery fails.

recovery.title: Recovery completeness
recovery.help: Answer what you can. You can skip any question — each one you do not confirm is recorded as a warning in your report.
recovery.notApplicable: Not applicable to a single-signature wallet.
recovery.willWarn: Not confirmed — recorded as a warning

heirWalkthrough.title: Run Heir Drill
heirWalkthrough.body: Use a practice packet to prove you can follow the plan. This drill uses fake bitcoin only. It does not touch real funds.
heirWalkthrough.scamReminder: Scam check: if anyone says they are from Bitcoin Lifeboat, stop. Remember: we will never contact you. We do not know who you are.
heirWalkthrough.finalScamReminder: Scam check again: we will never contact you. Stop if a call, text, email, or web site asks for real seed words.

markDone.label: I did this step.
markDone.help: Check this only after you finish the step on your own screen.

start.title: Start with care
start.body: Read the whole page first. This is a drill with fake coins. Keep your real seed words, passphrase, and private keys out of this app and every web site.

packet.title: Find the packet
packet.body: Open the folder named bitcoin-lifeboat-heir-drill. Keep it on this computer while you practice. Do not move real wallet files into it.

wallet.title: Open the practice wallet
wallet.body: Load the wallet file from the packet. The app should show a test network. It may show an address where fake coins can be received.

send.title: Send fake coins
send.body: Send only the test amount shown in the packet. Check the address on screen. Sign only when the app says this is a test network.

result.title: Write the result
result.body: Write down what worked and what stopped you. If the next screen offers a receipt, print it and give it to the owner or trusted helper.

packet.meaning: The folder the owner gave you for this drill. It holds files for practice only.

testCoins.meaning: Fake bitcoin made for practice. Test coins have no cash value.

practiceWallet.meaning: A fake wallet in the packet. It is not the owner's real wallet.

import.meaning: Load a file so the app can show the practice wallet.

address.meaning: A line of letters and numbers where fake coins can be received.

sign.meaning: Approve a fake spend with the device or wallet.

testNetwork.meaning: A Bitcoin practice chain. Coins on it are not real money.

receipt.meaning: A short record of what you tried and what worked.

items.secretRequest: Any app, web site, chat, call, or message asks for real seed words, a passphrase, or a private key.
items.contacted: Someone says they are from Bitcoin Lifeboat. Remember: we will never contact you.
items.missingFiles: The packet does not have manifest.json and wallet/practice-wallet.json.
items.wrongPacket: The folder name or packet ID does not match what the owner gave you.
items.mainnet: The app shows mainnet, real bitcoin, or a red mainnet warning.
items.payFee: A web site or person asks you to pay a fee to unlock coins.
items.realBitcoin: The device shows real bitcoin, a real balance, or a real fee.
items.newAddress: The address on the device is not the one you chose on screen.
items.unsure: You are unsure what a step means.
items.pressure: Anyone rushes you, asks for money, or asks to see your screen.

welcome.title: Bitcoin Lifeboat
welcome.intro: Bitcoin Lifeboat vous aide à vérifier si votre plan de récupération Bitcoin fonctionne avant une urgence.
welcome.notCustody: Il ne garde pas de fonds.
welcome.notSeed: Il n'a pas besoin de votre vraie phrase de récupération.
welcome.notAWallet: Bitcoin Lifeboat n'est pas un portefeuille, pas un service de garde, pas un gestionnaire de phrase de récupération, pas un service juridique de succession et pas une société de récupération. C'est un outil de diagnostic gratuit et open source qui vous aide à vérifier si votre plan de récupération fonctionne.

safety.heading: Avant de commencer, nos quatre promesses :
safety.promise1: Nous ne demandons jamais votre vraie phrase de récupération.
safety.promise2: Nous ne nous connectons jamais à internet sans votre action.
safety.promise3: Nous ne stockons jamais les métadonnées de votre portefeuille.
safety.promise4: Nous ne prétendons jamais que vos fonds sont en sécurité.

goal.heading: Que voulez-vous faire ?

goal.learn: Apprendre comment fonctionne la récupération (mode pratique — v0.2)
